messages:
alex: quick note — on the payments canary we observed partially unmasked emails in the request logs (local-part was visible). not a full breach but we should tighten inflight scrubbing before next rollout. :frowning:

maria: ah, thanks for catching. can you paste an example of what you saw and the scrub rules you want to change?

alex: payload snippet (sanitized):
```json
{
  "user": { "email": "alice.s*****@example.com" },
  "payment_method": "pm_1234"
}
```
we currently only run a post-ingest redact on top-level keys. that misses emails embedded in freeform text and bot replies. proposal: 1) inflight scrub step that normalizes and masks email local-parts and phone digits, 2) per-route expose toggle in Console that is quota-gated, 3) sampling shift: sample-per-route-per-hour instead of global percentage.

jordan: +1 for route-aware sampling. in practice, high-volume routes will drown out low-volume ones and we miss edge cases. route quota idea sounds good.

maria: curious about the UI implications — product wants an "Inspect" toggle today that flips for the whole org. per-route will be more work but less blast radius. can we make it gradual (beta in payments route first)? :eyes:

prateek: two operational notes: 1) inflight scrubbing adds CPU per-request if we run heavy regexes; prefer a streaming scan with lightweight heuristics plus a async deep-scan for sampled traces. 2) quota gating needs a hard cap + leaky-bucket so we don't exceed storage budget.

alex: exactly. suggested implementation: cheap regex to find email/phone tokens, mask local-part client-side style (first char + **** + domain), then enqueue sampled payloads for the deeper PII classifier offline. pseudoconfig below: 
```yaml
telemetry:
  inflight_scrub:
    enabled: true
    heuristics:
      email: true
      phone: true
      credit_card: false
  sampling:
    strategy: route_quota
    default_per_route_per_hour: 50
  expose_toggle:
    type: per_route
    quota_backend: leaky_bucket
```

eva: one question — are we keeping deterministic partial-hash ids for dedupe like we discussed before? that would mean hash(email) and only store short prefix. preserves linking while avoiding full PII.

jordan: i'd prefer partial-hash + salt per-org. store 8-char hex of hash(email+org_salt). that is reversible only if you keep salt, but we won't.

prateek: audit note: if we use salted hashes we need KMS integration for salt rotation and a migration plan. also update retention docs.

maria: ok can we make a short rollout plan? i think product will accept payments->canary then add two more routes next sprint.

alex: rollout plan suggestion:
- week 0: implement inflight cheap-scrub + route_quota sampling in staging, add console per-route toggle (default off)
- week 1: enable for payments route in internal org only, sample 100/hr, monitor ERR/latency/cost dashboards
- week 2: enable partial-hash dedupe for sampled traces, run privacy audit (legal + security)
- week 3: flip toggle for public canary (10% orgs) if metrics look good

maria: assign owners? alex for infra changes, prateek for cost/ops limits, jordan for hashing design, eva for privacy audit, product will coordinate rollout windows.

alex: taking infra owner. i'll open an RFC and a tiny changelist for the cheap regex lib.

prateek: i'll add leaky-bucket impl on the quota side and a dashboard for quota usage.

deploy-bot: canary job scheduled: telemetry-inflight-scrub/staging -> queued by alex.

maria: thanks — please tag #incidents if anything leaks. otherwise i'll track the RFC and coordinate with legal. :thumbsup:
